challenges.title: System Genesis: Root Protocol
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: Every HTML5 page must begin with <!DOCTYPE html>. This declaration tells the browser to interpret the code using modern web standards.
challenges.description: Your Task: The document is missing its essential first line. Add the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration to initialize the page correctly.

challenges.title: Data Stream Error: Unclosed Packet
challenges.learningConcept:
Concept: Most HTML elements, like paragraphs (

), require both an opening and a closing tag (

). This tells the browser where the element's content begins and ends.
challenges.description: Your Task: The paragraph tag in the code is not closed, which can corrupt the page layout. Provide the full, corrected line with the proper closing tag.

challenges.title: Signal Corruption: Image Packet
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: Image tags () must have an 'alt' attribute. This provides alternative text for screen readers and displays if the image fails to load.
challenges.description: Your Task: The image tag is missing its 'alt' attribute. Add the attribute to make the image accessible. The alt text can be 'logo'.

challenges.title: BOSS: The Architect's Gauntlet
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: A well-structured HTML document uses semantic tags to define its parts (like <header>, <footer>, <li>) and follows strict syntax rules for its elements.

stages.description: [STAGE 1/3] Your Task: A link (or 'anchor' tag) is broken. It's missing the 'href' attribute that tells it where to go. Fix the tag so it points to the homepage ('/').
[STAGE 2/3] Your Task: A list is structured incorrectly. Text inside an unordered list (<ul>) must be wrapped in list item (<li>) tags. Correct the line.
[STAGE 3/3] Your Task: The page's footer is using a generic <div> tag. For better structure and accessibility, it should use the semantic <footer> tag. Replace the div with the correct tag.

challenges.title: Firewall Alert: Unspecified Target
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: In CSS, to select and style all elements with a specific class, you must prefix the class name with a period (.).
challenges.description: Your Task: The style rule for 'error-text' isn't working because it's missing the period. Add the correct prefix to the selector.

challenges.title: Security Breach: Unique Identifier
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: To select and style a single element with a unique ID, you must prefix the ID name with a hash symbol (#).
challenges.description: Your Task: The style for the 'main-nav' ID is not being applied. The selector is missing the hash symbol. Correct the selector.

challenges.title: Targeting Matrix: Gravitational Constant
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: The 'text-align' property is used to control the horizontal alignment of text within an element.
challenges.description: Your Task: The text inside the h1 element is not centered. Choose the correct CSS property from the options below to center it.

challenges.title: BOSS: The Stylist's Challenge
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: Mastering CSS involves knowing the right properties to control color, layout (like grid and flexbox), and alignment.

stages.description: [STAGE 1/3] Your Task: A '.warning' element is supposed to be red, but it's invisible. The 'color' property is set incorrectly. Change the value to 'red'.
[STAGE 2/3] Your Task: A layout container is meant to use the CSS Grid system, but it's not working. The 'display' property is wrong. Change it to 'grid'.
[STAGE 3/3] Your Task: Items in a flexbox container need to be centered horizontally. 'align-items' handles vertical alignment. Use the correct property to center them along the main axis.

challenges.title: Logic Bomb: Assignment vs. Comparison
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: In JavaScript, a single equals sign (=) assigns a value. To compare if two values are equal, you must use the triple equals sign (===).
challenges.description: Your Task: The 'if' statement is broken because it's using an assignment operator instead of a comparison operator. Correct the line to properly compare 'x' to 10.

challenges.title: Subroutine Malfunction
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: To run, or 'call', a function in JavaScript, you must type its name followed by parentheses ().
challenges.description: Your Task: The code references the 'showWelcomeMessage' function, but doesn't actually run it. Add parentheses to the end of the line to call the function.

challenges.title: BOSS: The De-Bugger's Final Test
challenges.learningConcept: Concept: Debugging JavaScript often involves fixing selectors to interact with HTML, ensuring functions return values, and correctly setting up event listeners.

stages.description: [STAGE 1/3] Your Task: The code is trying to select an HTML element with an ID of 'alert-banner', but the selector is wrong. Remember that ID selectors in JavaScript (like in CSS) need a '#' prefix.
[STAGE 2/3] Your Task: The 'getUser' function is supposed to provide a username, but it doesn't return anything. Add the 'return' keyword to send the username value back.

[STAGE 3/3] Your Task: An event listener is set up to run a 'handleClick' function when a button is clicked, but the syntax is incomplete. Pass the function name as the second argument to 'addEventListener'.
